query: For high-entropy-alloy materials intended for self-lubricating moving components, what single intervention could reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the untreated alloy, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites prior evidence supporting it, and proposes an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 0.5-1 wt% of graphene nanoplatelets as a solid lubricant to the high-entropy alloy (HEA) CoCrFeMnNi will reduce the coefficient of friction and wear rate across a wide service-temperature range.
generation.intervention: Addition of 0.5-1 wt% of graphene nanoplatelets as a solid lubricant
generation.conditions: Service temperature range: -20°C to 500°C, sliding speed: 0.1-1 m/s, normal load: 10-100 N
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a thin, stable tribofilm containing graphene nanoplatelets
generation.mechanism: The graphene nanoplatelets reduce friction and wear by forming a low-shear-strength tribofilm that prevents direct metal-to-metal contact, while the HEA substrate provides high strength and toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: 25-45% reduction in coefficient of friction and 45-65% reduction in wear rate compared to the untreated HEA
generation.boundary: Service temperature range: -20°C to 500°C, sliding speed: 0.1-1 m/s, normal load: 10-100 N
generation.uncertainty: The actual reduction in coefficient of friction and wear rate may vary depending on the optimization of the dispersion and stability of graphene nanoplatelets in the HEA matrix

falsification_experiment.design: Tribological testing of the graphene nanoplatelet-reinforced HEA against a steel counterface under various service conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured coefficient of friction and wear rate are not significantly reduced compared to the untreated HEA, the hypothesis is falsified
